summary: Discovery call to understand Zephyra's migration from OpenAI-hosted + on-prem vLLM/TGI stack to Redwood (hosted/dedicated/private). Key concerns: eval parity, latency/cost tradeoffs, KMS/audit logs, SOC2, pilot scope. Agreed to run parity benchmarks and exchange security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hi everyone, thanks for — hey, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. Marcus, our SE, is here. Can you, uh, introduce yourselves quick?
[00:10] Aisha Khan: Yeah hi, i'm Aisha, head of ML ops at Zephyra, we run most of our stuff on OpenAI's hosted API but we also have an on-prem vLLM/TGI cluster for cost-sensitive inference.
[00:22] Carlos Mendez: Carlos here, CTO, short on time but want to make sure we cover compliance and estimate cost delta.
[00:28] Marcus Reed: Hey all, Marcus — SE, nice to meet you. Quick note, i'll be the one doing the parity bench if we move forward.
[00:34] Ravi Patel: Ravi, infra engineer, i manage our vLLM fleet and networking, curious about VPC/private options.
[00:40] Lena Park: Great. Goal for today: understand your stack, run constraints, and what success looks like if you were to move to Redwood — hosted, dedicated, or private. Also, surface any blockers.
[00:51] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. Brief context — we started on OpenAI API for chat features, but token costs spiked. So we built vLLM/TGI on prem and got costs down but we lose some of the managed stuff — monitoring, SLOs, rollout tools. We want something that balances cost and reliability without rebuilding ops.
[01:10] Marcus Reed: Understood. Can you share current qps, average latency targets, and your typical model footprints?
[01:16] Aisha Khan: For production: 10 qps sustained on the high tier, tails up to 50 qps during spikes. Latency target is p95 under 350ms for short completion tasks (~256 tokens). Models: mixture — GPT-3.5-like open checkpoints and some in-house fine-tuned Mistral variants, coupled with TGI runtime for some endpoints.
[01:36] Carlos Mendez: And importantly, we need audit logs and KMS integration for customer data residency reasons. SOC2 is a must.
[01:44] Lena Park: Totally — Redwood offers hosted for quick move, dedicated pools for predictable throughput, and private deployments for VPC/on-prem with KM S options. We are SOC2 and have enterprise compliance docs, will share.
[01:56] Aisha Khan: When you say private, do you mean fully air-gapped on prem? Because for some customers we need that.
[02:03] Marcus Reed: We support VPC-hosted private control plane and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments — there are some additional integration steps (KMS/HSM) and ops handover. We can map a checklist.
[02:14] Ravi Patel: What about model compatibility — will our TGI/vLLM models run unchanged? We're using custom kernels, kv-cache tuning, and quantized weights.
[02:23] Marcus Reed: Short answer: most architectures run but there are gotchas. vLLM/TGI runtime differences, custom kernels, and quantization formats can require conversion. We'll run a compatibility scan. Our runtime supports common quant formats but some vendor-specific kernels need adaptation.
[02:40] Aisha Khan: Do you do eval parity tests? We worry about slight quality regressions when we quantize or change runtimes.
[02:46] Marcus Reed: Yes — part of our onboarding is an eval harness that runs your prompt sets and compares outputs across metrics: semantic fidelity, token-level diffs, latency distribution. We usually do a small canary before full cutover.
[02:57] Carlos Mendez: Also curious about failover — if you have a hosted region outage, can requests fallback to a dedicated pool or to a lower-cost model?
[03:07] Lena Park: Yep, smart routing + fallbacks are built in. Policies can prefer latency or cost, and we can fallback to compatible model variants (e.g., quantized variant) or to another region.
[03:18] Ravi Patel: Network egress is another cost center for us. If you host in our VPC, how does egress billing look?
[03:25] Marcus Reed: For private and dedicated, egress is typically handled in the customer's cloud account — we can provide options. For hosted API, egress is on us but included in pricing tiers. We'll include egress scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[03:38] Aisha Khan: Ok, what about benchmarks — we run vLLM with pinned GPUs and batching; our latency's dependent on batch sizes. What's Redwood's batching behavior?
[03:47] Marcus Reed: Our serving runtime does continuous batching with workload-aware sizing. You can configure per-route batching SLOs. For tight p95 constraints we can favor low-latency paths that sacrifice throughput; for cost we can increase batching. We'll show empirical numbers in the benchmark.
[04:02] Carlos Mendez: Who typically lands on dedicated vs private?
[04:06] Lena Park: Dedicated is common for customers who want predictable throughput and isolation without fully managing infra. Private is for customers needing strict network controls or air-gapped. Hosted is for fastest time-to-value.
[04:16] Ravi Patel: How does model versioning and rollouts work? We do staged rollouts, canary, rollback.
[04:22] Marcus Reed: Redwood Console supports rollouts — canary percentages, automatic rollback based on error or quality regressions (we tie evals to rollouts). You can pin model versions per route.
[04:33] Aisha Khan: Security details — SSO, RBAC, audit logs. We need to pass an internal security review.
[04:39] Lena Park: We'll send our security pack (SOC2, pen test summary, incident response). For private we integrate with your SSO (SAML/OIDC) and KMS for key ownership.
[04:50] Carlos Mendez: Great. On the cost side, can you ballpark token/unit prices vs our current OpenAI spend if we go hosted?
[04:58] Lena Park: Ballpark depends on model choice and throughput, but hosted often reduces ops cost; dedicated reduces per-token cost at commit levels. We'll prepare a tailored estimate once we have traces and model mix.
[05:10] Aisha Khan: For the parity benchmark, i want to run our standard prompt set — a mix of short completions and longer multi-turn chat. We'll expect logs and diff outputs.
[05:20] Marcus Reed: Perfect. We'll run three comparisons: current OpenAI hosted outputs, your on-prem vLLM/TGI, and Redwood hosted/dedicated/private variants. We'll collect semantic score, token diffs, latency percentiles.
[05:33] Ravi Patel: Any known incompatibilities with TGI endpoints? We use custom TGI handlers for streaming and tools calling.
[05:41] Marcus Reed: Streaming is supported, including tool-calls; however, small differences in streaming chunking and message IDs can occur. We'll adapt the TGI handlers or provide a shim if needed.
[05:53] Aisha Khan: About data retention and logs — can we set short retention for PII?
[05:58] Lena Park: Yes, retention is configurable per customer and per route in dedicated/private. Hosted has retention tiers and you can request short retention for sensitive data.
[06:08] Carlos Mendez: Are you able to bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM?
[06:12] Marcus Reed: Yes, for private deployments we support KMS integrations and can integrate with an HSM-backed key store for encryption at rest.
[06:19] Aisha Khan: Okay, next — SLA and SLOs. We need 99.9% uptime on critical routes.
[06:24] Lena Park: Dedicated comes with SLA and SLOs; hosted has standard uptime commitments. We can add premium SLA on an enterprise contract.
[06:33] Ravi Patel: Let's talk pilot scope — how long and what metrics?
[06:37] Lena Park: Typical pilot is 4 weeks: week 1-2 parity and performance tests, week 3 canary traffic (small %), week 4 ramp and handover. Metrics: semantic parity, latency p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, error rate.
[06:49] Aisha Khan: Sounds reasonable. Any pre-reqs from our side?
[06:52] Marcus Reed: We'll need sample traces, model files if you want us to run your actual checkpoints, and network access to any private resources if doing private deploy.
[07:02] Carlos Mendez: For model files, we have some licensed weights — distribution restrictions apply. Can you handle license compliance?
[07:09] Marcus Reed: We have a model onboarding checklist and NDA-friendly transfer procedures. For restricted weights, we can run benchmarks in your environment or under a limited access agreement.
[07:20] Aisha Khan: Great. On the timeline, we'd like to pick a path before end of Q1.
[07:24] Lena Park: That's doable. If benchmarks look good, we can get a pilot contract signed in 2–3 weeks after benchmark.
[07:31] Ravi Patel: One more thing — observability. We use Datadog and Sentry. Can Redwood integrate with those?
[07:36] Marcus Reed: Yes, we export metrics/traces and have integrations for Datadog, Prometheus, and webhook alerts. Error export to Sentry-compatible formats is doable.
[07:48] Aisha Khan: Any friction moving away from OpenAI — API changes?
[07:52] Lena Park: We provide SDKs and a compatibility layer; depending on your usage of OpenAI-specific endpoints (like certain chat schema), you may need small adapters. We can provide a migration guide.
[08:03] Carlos Mendez: Pricing question again — if we keep heavy callers on our on-prem vLLM and move burst traffic to Redwood dedicated, is hybrid supported?
[08:11] Marcus Reed: Absolutely. We support hybrid routing — on prem for steady-state heavy traffic + dedicated for burst capacity, or hosted for overflow.
[08:21] Aisha Khan: Alright. Let's capture the concrete next steps so nothing falls through.
[08:26] Lena Park: I'll repeat: Marcus will get the benchmark harness ready and run parity with your traces — he'll need the traces and any model files you permit. I'll send the security/compliance pack and pricing. We aim to review bench results the week of 12/21.
[08:40] Aisha Khan: Confirmed. I'll upload traces and nominate a contact (Ravi) to work with Marcus.
[08:46] Ravi Patel: Yep i'll be primary infra contact.
[08:50] Carlos Mendez: I'll review the security pack once you send it.
[08:54] Lena Park: Great. Anything else?
[08:56] Aisha Khan: Maybe one more question — how do you handle model drift/quality monitoring post-deploy?
[09:02] Marcus Reed: We have a quality monitoring pipeline that runs prompt sets continuously and flags regressions. We also support custom eval hooks to run your own evaluators and tie alerts to rollbacks.
[09:15] Lena Park: Perfect. If no more questions, we'll wrap — thanks everyone. We'll send notes and action items.
[09:21] Carlos Mendez: Thanks — appreciate the clarity.
[09:24] Aisha Khan: Thanks all, talk soon.
[09:27] Ravi Patel: Thanks.
[09:30] Lena Park: Bye all.

Notes: Transcript contains minor transcription errors typical of automated tools; product names like TGI/vLLM may be transcribed variably.
